overview: Chatham Rock Phosphate is a pre-revenue mineral development company seeking to build phosphate mining/rehabilitation projects on the Chatham Rise seabed off New Zealand and at Makatea Island in French Polynesia (via its Avenir Makatea subsidiary), with a small early-stage Queensland (Korella) land-based phosphate interest. The company holds a 20-year Minerals Mining Permit for the Chatham Rise (820 sq km) but cannot mine without a Marine Consent that was refused in 2015 and has not been re-granted. Incorporated in British Columbia, historically dual-listed TSX-V/NZX and reporting in CAD, it delisted from the TSX-V in July 2026 and is now pursuing a direct NZX listing after its NZX shares were suspended from trading on August 3, 2026.

business_model.summary: Pre-revenue exploration/development company with zero product sales. The entire business model is optionality on regulatory approval (Marine Consent for Chatham Rise, Mining Concession for Makatea) followed by capital-intensive construction and seabed/land mining of rock phosphate for fertiliser feedstock. Funded almost entirely by dilutive equity placements and, since 2025, a convertible working-capital loan from a single financing partner (Wetstone Global) that can convert into up to 75% of the Chatham Rise subsidiary.
business_model.customer_type: None currently; end customers would eventually be fertiliser manufacturers/agricultural distributors (B2B commodity sale) if mining commences
business_model.geographic_mix: Mineral interests in New Zealand (Chatham Rise, ~$4.6m carrying value), French Polynesia (Makatea, ~$1.9m carrying value), and Queensland Australia (Korella, ~$0.16m carrying value); corporate head office functions split between Vancouver, Canada and Wellington, New Zealand

main_competitors: other conventional land-based phosphate rock miners
competitive_position.market_position: Not a competitive participant in the phosphate market - the company has never produced or sold a tonne of phosphate rock. Any 'position' is purely optionality on an undeveloped, unpermitted deposit versus established low-cost conventional producers who dominate global supply

moat_factors.description: Holds one of the few seabed Minerals Mining Permits on the Chatham Rise, but the permit is worthless without Marine Consent, which was refused once and remains ungranted more than a decade later
Company markets its (unmined) phosphate as low-cadmium relative to some conventional rock sources, a potential differentiator for organic/premium fertiliser markets if ever produced at scale
Years of resource definition and studies could shorten path to production for a well-capitalised acquirer, which is part of the rationale for the Wetstone earn-in structure

weaknesses: No revenue, no production, no proven path to a granted Marine Consent after a decade of failed attempts
Chronic going-concern qualification and reliance on continuous, highly dilutive micro-cap equity placements (raises of CAD$130-160k at $0.05/share)
Extreme balance-sheet fragility: cash of only CAD$35k-71k against a company with a CAD$6.7m intangible mineral asset carrying value
Newly delisted from TSX-V and NZX trading itself is currently suspended (since Aug 2026) pending a direct-listing application, materially impairing liquidity and price discovery
Core financing partner (Wetstone Global) can end up owning up to 75% of the key Chatham Rise subsidiary, diluting economic exposure of CRP shareholders to the flagship asset

growth_drivers: Successful re-application for Marine Consent on the Chatham Rise (single largest potential re-rating catalyst)
Progress of the Makatea Mining Concession application in French Polynesia, with management previously flagging a public enquiry and potential concession grant in FY2025-26
Wetstone Global earn-in/investment agreement providing staged working capital and a path to project-level construction funding without requiring CRP-level equity at every step
Successful NZX direct-listing application restoring tradability and market access post TSX-V delisting
Rising global fertiliser demand and firm phosphate rock benchmark pricing (Morocco FOB ~US$150-160/mt through 2025-26) improving underlying project economics if permits are eventually granted
Potential farm-down or sale of project interests (explicitly flagged by the Directors as a going-concern mitigant) to advance commercialisation without full CRP-level capital commitment
Korella (Queensland) low-cost, near-surface phosphate exploration as an early-cash-flow diversification option outside the Marine Consent bottleneck

business.description: The entire Chatham Rise asset value (~$4.6m of $6.7m total mineral property interest) is contingent on a Marine Consent that has already been refused once (2015) and a related change-of-conditions application refused again in 2023/2024; there is no guarantee of ever obtaining consent
Zero revenue for the company's entire history; value is entirely speculative and concentrated in unpermitted mineral interests

Financing is now dependent on one interested party/lender whose loan can convert into up to 75% of the key operating subsidiary, creating both key-person/counterparty risk and severe dilution/control risk for CRP shareholders

Group has not met minimum work programme commitments under Minerals Mining Permit 55549; NZP&M has discretion to decline future permit applications or revoke the permit for non-compliance, though it has confirmed no action is currently underway

financial.description: Auditor's report (FY2025) includes a material uncertainty related to going concern; current liabilities have exceeded current assets in every recent period (deficit of ~$459k at Dec 2025) and cash balances are frequently below CAD$50k

Share count has grown from ~85m (FY2023) to over 115m (Dec 2025) via repeated small private placements at deeply discounted prices (CAD$0.05-0.12/share), plus warrant and option overhangs (~28m warrants, ~11m options outstanding)
Reports in CAD with functional currencies in NZD, AUD and XPF across subsidiaries; no hedging, so FX volatility affects reported equity/deficit each period
Amounts due to directors (~$222k at Dec 2025) with directors agreeing not to demand repayment for 12 months - a going-concern support measure but also a sign of cash strain

regulatory.risk: Marine Consent / EEZ Act regulatory bar
regulatory.description: New Zealand's Environmental Protection Authority previously found seabed mining would cause significant and permanent adverse effects; environmental and iwi/community opposition remains a structural barrier to re-application success
Makatea project requires a Mining Concession from French Polynesia's Council of Ministers following a Public Enquiry process; outcome and timing remain uncertain despite years of consultation

TSX-V delisting (effective July 31, 2026) and subsequent NZX trading suspension (from Aug 3, 2026) pending a direct listing application creates uncertainty over when/if normal trading resumes and shifts oversight fully to NZX

macro.description: Global phosphate rock prices (Morocco FOB benchmark ~US$150-160/mt) are subject to agricultural cycles, fertiliser subsidy policy (e.g., India), and competition from low-cost incumbent producers (Morocco's OCP, etc.)

macro.risk: Capital markets access for micro-cap explorers
macro.description: As a sub-CAD$0.05 micro-cap with going-concern doubt, CRP is acutely exposed to any tightening in risk appetite for speculative resource juniors

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global phosphate rock market outlook is moderately constructive - benchmark Morocco FOB prices held broadly stable/firm through 2025-2026 (roughly US$150-160/mt), supported by agricultural demand and subsidy-backed demand in markets like India; the market is forecast to grow at a mid-single-digit CAGR through the late 2020s
macro_factors.cyclicality: High at the company level (pre-revenue, entirely dependent on financing cycles and permit outcomes) though the underlying commodity market itself is only moderately cyclical, tracking global agricultural/fertiliser demand
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Indirect but meaningful - CRP relies on speculative risk capital and a convertible loan (Wetstone) with a step-up interest rate (10% rising to 12.5%+ over time), so higher rates raise the cost and reduce availability of financing
key_input_costs: Vessel/marine construction and mobilisation costs (Chatham Rise)
Corporate/compliance costs across three jurisdictions (Canada, New Zealand, France/French Polynesia)

recent_developments.event: NZX trading suspended from August 3, 2026 after TSX-V delisting removed CRP's foreign exempt issuer status; company has begun the process to make NZX its primary/direct listing
Delisted from the TSX Venture Exchange effective July 31, 2026 following shareholder approval, ending the long-standing dual TSX-V/NZX listing

Chatham Rock and Wetstone Global amended their investment agreement, raising the maximum equity stake in subsidiary Chatham Rock Phosphate (NZ) Limited that Wetstone's limited-recourse loan can convert into from 70% to 75%
Chatham Rock and Wetstone Global entered definitive documents for financing of the Chatham Rise project (following the August 2025 term sheet/loan agreement)
NZX announcement clarifying terms of the Wetstone loan agreement originally announced without proper disclosure timing

Sale of a further partial interest reducing Avenir Makatea Pty Ltd's effective ownership to ~70% and related Australian subsidiary/Organoselenium interest changes, continuing a pattern of partial divestments to raise cash and streamline the portfolio
Closed a non-brokered private placement of 3,162,995 shares at CAD$0.05/share for gross proceeds of CAD$158,150
Granted 8,750,000 fully vested share options to directors at $0.054/share exercise price, a large share-based payment charge (~$331k) relative to the size of the company

Secured a USD$150,000 loan from Wetstone Global at 10% interest (stepping up to 12.5%+ over time), secured against the Chatham Rise project assets, convertible into equity of the NZ subsidiary - the seed of the now-larger Wetstone financing relationship
Closed a non-brokered private placement of 2,764,003 shares at CAD$0.05/share for gross proceeds of CAD$138,200

guidance.as_of: Q3 FY2026 (three/nine months ended December 31, 2025) unaudited interim financial statements, approved March 2, 2026

items.period: FY2026 and beyond until Marine Consent/Mining Concession granted
items.notes: Company remains pre-revenue; no revenue guidance has ever been issued as production is contingent on unresolved regulatory approvals

items.target: 12 months from date of financial statement approval, contingent on continued equity raises, Director forbearance on repayment, and completion of Wetstone due diligence/definitive agreement
items.period: Rolling 12-month basis (most recently reaffirmed in Dec-2025 quarterly, approved March 2026)
items.notes: Management states expenditure is 'scalable' and can be curtailed if no further funding is obtained; explicitly flags farm-down/asset sale as a fallback

items.target: Grant of Mining Concession expected "late FY2025-26"
items.vs_prior: maintained from prior filings, though timeline has slipped across multiple years historically
items.notes: Management has repeatedly flagged this timeline in prior annual/interim reports without the concession yet being confirmed granted in the extracted filings reviewed

items.target: No material near-term production capex guided; ongoing minimum exploration/evaluation spend only
items.notes: Long-term permit work programme requires average NZD 2 million/year of survey and sampling spend once triggered (120 months from permit commencement), but this is contingent on reaching later permit milestones not yet triggered

guidance.management_commentary: Directors continue to characterise the Chatham Rise mineral interest as not impaired, citing valid tenure, planned further exploration spend, and studies suggesting continued commercial viability, while simultaneously disclosing material uncertainty about going concern and financing. CEO Chris Castle and CFO Robyn Hamilton have signed off FY2025 and interim statements reiterating dependence on the Wetstone financing relationship and further capital raises.

bull_case: Successful re-application and grant of Marine Consent for the Chatham Rise would unlock a large, already-permitted (mining permit) seabed phosphate resource with a 20-year mining permit runway to 2033
Wetstone Global's staged financing/earn-in structure could fund the Chatham Rise project to construction without requiring CRP to raise all capital via dilutive equity at the parent level

Firm global phosphate rock pricing (Morocco FOB benchmark holding near US$150-160/mt) and steady agricultural fertiliser demand support project economics if the deposit is ever brought into production

Multiple call options in one vehicle - Chatham Rise (NZ), Makatea (French Polynesia), and Korella (Australia) - any one of which reaching a positive permitting outcome could re-rate the stock materially off its current sub-CAD$0.05 base
Low absolute market capitalisation and share price mean even a partial de-risking event (e.g., Makatea concession grant) could produce an outsized percentage re-rating
bear_case: A decade-plus track record of failed/declined regulatory applications (2015 Marine Consent refusal, 2023/2024 change-of-conditions refusal) suggests structural, not just procedural, opposition to Chatham Rise seabed mining

Recurring going-concern qualification, chronic negative working capital, and reliance on sub-CAD$0.06/share placements point to a company perpetually on the edge of insolvency with severe, ongoing dilution

Wetstone Global's ability to convert its loan into up to 75% of the key operating subsidiary means existing CRP shareholders could see their economic interest in the flagship Chatham Rise asset heavily diluted even if the project eventually succeeds

TSX-V delisting and the subsequent NZX trading suspension (since August 2026) materially impair liquidity, price discovery, and the ability of existing holders to exit, independent of project fundamentals

Zero revenue after many years of exploration spend, with the company's entire ~CAD$6.7m of assets consisting of intangible, unpermitted mineral property interests that could be impaired to near-zero if any of the Marine Consent, Mining Concession, or Wetstone financing paths fail
